title: Infra: GPU Fleet & Capacity + Cloud Accounts, IaC Modules, CI/CD Playbook (Consolidated)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This consolidated playbook documents Redwood Inference's operational standards and runbooks for GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines and day-2 runbooks. It is the canonical reference for infra engineers responsible for procurement, provisioning and operational health of GPU-backed inference capacity.

Goal and intended audience:
- Audience: infra engineers, SREs, platform engineers, and on-call engineers who operate GPU-backed clusters and the IaC/CI processes that manage them.
- Goals: reduce mean-time-to-recovery (MTTR) for capacity incidents, standardize IaC modules and pipelines, maintain predictable cost and utilization, and provide clear runbooks for routine scale and incident responses.

Owners and contacts:
- Primary owner: Infra Capacity Team (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Secondary: GPU Fleet & Scheduling (owner: Jordan Kim)
- Oncall rotation: infra-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Pager escalation: Level 1 -> Level 2 -> Eng SRE Lead (see Escalation matrix section)

SLOs and operational targets:
- Median GPU utilization per pool: 60% (target range 50-70%).
- Capacity headroom: maintain >= 20% spare capacity for burst traffic during business hours.
- Provisioning SLA for new reserved nodes: 6 hours for warm pools, 48 hours for new hardware requests (procurement).
- Incident MTTR target (capacity-related): 60 minutes for transient autoscale fixes; 6 hours for hardware/node replacement.

Capacity planning process (quarterly):
1. Collect usage data: run 90/95/99th percentile token and request rates per pool for the trailing 90 days (Prometheus/Grafana dashboards).
2. Forecast growth: apply linear and opportunistic growth scenarios (nominal +20% q/q, peak +40% q/q) and identify required additional vGPU-hours.
3. Translate to nodes: use standard SKU sizing table (see Fleet sizing) to map vGPU-hours to node counts per region.
4. Budget check & procurement: raise infra budget request ticket and notify finance.
5. Provision & verify: run e2e smoke tests and integration tests on new capacity before promoting to production weight.

Fleet sizing methodology:
- Inputs: avg tokens/sec, avg sequence length, concurrency distribution, model memory footprint (GB), quantization profile.
- Example sizing table (reference):
| SKU | GPU mem | vGPU profile | baseline throughput (tokens/s) | recommended concurrency | notes |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| a2-standard-1 (A100 80GB) | 80GB | fp16/4-bit | 1200 | 24 | Best for large context models
| p4d-24xlarge (H100 equivalent) | 96GB | q4_k_m | 1400 | 32 | High throughput, high cost
| g5dn.xlarge | 16GB | fp16 | 200 | 4 | Cost-efficient for embeddings / small models

- Sizing formula (text): node_count = ceil((forecast_peak_tokens_per_sec / node_baseline_throughput) * safety_factor), where safety_factor=1.25 for regional pools.

Cloud accounts and networking standards:
- Account structure: one infra master account per cloud provider + bounded project accounts per region/environment (prod/stage/dev).
- VPCs and subnets:
  - Production GPU pools run in dedicated VPCs per region with private subnets for nodes and a control subnet for control-plane services.
  - Egress: egress via NAT gateway with egress logging enabled.
  - Peering: management control plane uses VPC peering/shared VPC (AWS Transit Gateway) for required access; avoid cross-region peering for data plane traffic.
- Security & IAM:
  - Principle of least privilege for service roles.
  - Use short-lived instance credentials where supported; enforce IAM permission boundaries for IaC runners.
- Tagging convention (required for cost attribution):
  - tag:team = infra
  - tag:env = prod|stage|dev
  - tag:pool = gpu-inference-<model-class>
  - tag:owner = <oncall-owner>

Terraform / IaC module standards:
- Module catalog (high-level):
  - redwood/gpu-node: manages GPU node ASG/instance template, drivers, and telemetry agents.
  - redwood/gpu-pool: logical pool consisting of node groups, autoscaler config and scheduling constraints.
  - redwood/network-vpc: VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT gateways.
  - redwood/iam-service-account: standardized IAM policies and service accounts for runners.
- Module interface guidelines:
  - Inputs must be small and explicit (strings, lists), prefer computed outputs only when required.
  - Versioning: semantic versioning tags (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). New major version requires ADR.
  - Tests: each module must include terratest integration tests and a small plan-only workflow in CI.

Example module usage snippet (Terraform):
```hcl
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-infra/terraform-modules.git//gpu-pool?ref=v1.3.0"
  name   = "gpu-inference-west-1"
  env    = "prod"
  sku    = "p4d-24xlarge"
  min_size = 4
  max_size = 64
  tags = { team = "infra" }
}
```

CI/CD and build conventions for IaC and fleet images:
- Pipeline stages (Terraform modules):
  1. lint (tflint, tfsec)
  2. fmt/checks
  3. plan (isolated environment with remote state read-only)
  4. automated policy checks (OPA/Gatekeeper)
  5. manual approval (for prod) -> apply
- Immutable build images:
  - All node images are built in Packer pipelines, published to private image registries, and promoted through dev->stage->prod channels.
  - Image build pipeline must install GPU drivers, NVidia container runtime, telemetry agents, and run the smoke test suite.
- Example CI YAML fragment (conceptual):
```yaml
jobs:
  - name: terraform-plan
    image: hashicorp/terraform:1.5
    steps:
      - run: tflint ./modules/gpu-pool
      - run: terraform init -backend-config=ci-backend.hcl
      - run: terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -out=plan.out
```

Deployment and rollout guidance:
- Canary policy: deploy new pool weights in 4 steps (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with 30-minute observation windows.
- Autoscaling policy defaults: target 60% GPU utilization, scale_out cooldown 120s, scale_in cooldown 600s.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants (q4k, 4-bit) when pool utilization exceeds 90% unless overridden by route policy.

Runbooks (operational):
- Incident: GPU pool OOM / node-level GPU failure
  1. Identify affected pool from alert (alert:gpu_node_gpu_error_count > 0).
  2. Run diagnostics: ssh to node via bastion, check nvidia-smi, dmesg, journalctl -u kubelet.
  3. If transient, cordon & drain node:
     - kubectl cordon <node>
     - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
  4. Replace node from autoscale group (terminate instance to cycle) or increase desired_count if under-provisioned.
  5. Validate: check pod restarts, model-serving latencies, and queue length.
  6. Postmortem: file incident report, record root cause, notify capacity planning.
- Runbook: Draining and safely replacing a GPU node (routine maintenance)
  1. Schedule maintenance window if draining > 2 nodes in same pool.
  2. Notify oncall and downstream teams via #infra-announce.
  3. kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  4. Verify pods relocated and scheduler evicted: kubectl get pods -o wide -A | grep <node>
  5. Reboot or replace node image via ASG/instance template update and monitor logs.

Monitoring, dashboards and alerts:
- Dashboards to maintain:
  - GPU Fleet Overview: per-pool utilization, headroom, memory pressure, queue depth.
  - Scheduling & Eviction: pod preemption, pending pods > 5m, scheduling latency.
  - Cost: per-pool hourly burn rate, reserved vs on-demand ratio.
- Key alerts (examples):
  - gpu_pool_high_utilization: fired when median utilization > 90% for 10m
  - gpu_node_driver_failures: > 3 failures in 5m
  - pending_pods_backlog: average pending pods > 50 for 5m

Escalation matrix (short):
- Pager -> oncall infra -> GPU fleet engineer -> Eng SRE lead -> CTO (if > 8h outage).

Appendix:
- Useful commands:
  - Check GPU: ssh bastion; nvidia-smi -a
  - Drain node: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  - Terraform plan: terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars -out=plan.out
- PromQL examples:
  - GPU utilization panel: avg by (pool) (rate(gpu_utilization_seconds_total[5m]))*100
